RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, the May 22, 2007/Jyaistha 1, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Civil Aviation; Corporate Affairs; Culture; Finance;
Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and
Natural Gas; Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
209
Promotion of literature on art and
culture in Goa
*661. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether any schemes are in force
for the promotion of literature on art and
culture in Goa;
(b) what are the essential features of
the schemes;
(c) the projects undertaken/
implemented under the schemes during the
last three years in the State; and
(d) the details of financial assistance
granted to the State during the last three
years, year-wise?
Moderation in growth of credit to
high risk sectors
*662. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the banks
have been asked to moderate growth of
credit to high risk sectors;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that  a number
of the Public Sector Banks have objected
to it; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Conversion of loans in to equity in
CPSEs
*663. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of the amount of
outstanding loans to CPSEs converted into
equity as part of the revival plan
recommended by BRPSE during the last
two years;
(b) the details of the fresh equity
infusion into CPSEs as part of revival;
(c) what is the current worth of
Government's fresh equity investment and
converted equity during the last two years;
(d) the details of the comparative worth,
if the worth has gone down; and
(e) if not, how much dividend have
Government earned over the last two years
over such equity in the CPSEs?

210
Development of tourist centres in
Rajasthan
†*664. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will
the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Central Government
have prepared any draft for development
of various tourist centres in Rajasthan;
(b) whether Government have any plan
to develop new tourist centres also
alongwith the development of old tourist
centres;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the names of the districts in
Rajasthan for whose development
proposals have been submitted to the
Central Government from the State
Government and the names of the tourist
centres Central Government have planned
to develop out of them and the target fixed
for completion of those plans alongwith
the details thereof?
Labour Law Compliance Report
*665. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: W ill the Minister of
CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to
 state:
(a) whether the Institute of Company
Secretaries of India under his Ministry is
working on the concept of Labour Audit or
Labour Law  Compliance Report being
made compulsory of companies;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the proposed Labour Audit or the
Labour Law Compliance Report will cover
which Labour Acts?
Identification of unexplored tourist
spots
*666. DR. ABHISHEK MANU
SINGHVI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that during 2006
the tourist arrival touched 4.43 million after
having stagnated around two million for
decades; and
(b) if so, whether Government would
identify more tourist spots which are
unexplored in States like Bihar (Buddhist
destinations), Himachal Pradesh
(Dharamshala, Chamundadevi, Chamba,
etc.), Uttarakhand (Pauri, Tehri,
Devprayag, Ranikhet), Punjab (Hindu
Temples and Sikh Gurudwaras) and
Haryana (Panipat, Kurukshetra, etc.) under
the umbrella of 'Incredible India' so that
target foreign budget groups may visit India
in large numbers?
Raising investment in petrochemical
sector
*667. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government approved the
National Policy on Petrochemicals which
outlines the broad contours to raise
investment in the sector so that India does
not miss the opportunity in the Asian
petrochemical boom;
(b) whether Government will introduce
necessary incentives to boost private

investment in petroleum, chemical and
petrochemical investment regions;
(c) whether ONGC worked out
investment of Rs. 18,000 crore for
exploration and production of oil and gas
in the current financial year 2007-08;
(d) what are the main projects that
would be undertaken; and
(e) by when the implementation of these
projects would start?
Construction of new dam in place of
Mullaperiyar dam in Kerala

Minister of WATER RESOURCES be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of dams in the country
which are more than 100 years old;
(b) whether any study has been
conducted on the safety of these dams;
(c) if so, the details thereof;

Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas;

Total number of questions —155
1175
Emergency landing at
IGIA
5052. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL:
SHRI RAJEEV
CHANDRASEKHAR:
SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether any investigation has been
conducted into the emergency landing of
two Air India aircrafts at the Indira Gandhi
International Airport in Delhi on  April 9,
2007;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action taken, if any, thereon?
Ageing aircrafts
†5053. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that most of the
aeroplanes of Air India, Indian and Alliance
Air have become old and worn-out due to
which the possibility of occurrence of any
kind of dangerous accident at any time
cannot be ruled out;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
Government are still in a state of confusion
and indecision in the matter of removing
the old and worn-out aeroplanes from the
fleet and including new aeroplanes in the
fleet; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and
Government's views in this regard?
Regularization of casual
labour
5054. SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Indian Airlines has decided
to regularize the casual labour working in
the Southern Region;
(b) if so, by when this decision is likely
to be implemented; and
(c) whether Government are considering
to implement similar guidelines in other
regions as well?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

1176
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Worker related issues of Air India and
Indian
5055. SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government will hold
consultations with the unions and
associations of workers and employees of
both Indian and Air India before the
proposed mergers; and
(b) what are the proposals of
Government to clinch the worker related
issues of both the companies?
Replacement of obsolete aircrafts
†5056. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of aircrafts being used
by Air India and Indian which are more
than 15 years old;
(b) the details of these aircrafts;
(c) the period for which an aircraft is
considered fit for use, as per the norms
fixed; and
(d) the steps being taken by
Government to replace the aircrafts which
have become obsolete?
Special air-package for HP and JK
5057. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
introduce special air-packages other than
holiday packages and lower fare schemes,
in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and
Kashmir in view of the potential for tourism;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when this special air-package is
likely to be introduced in these States?
Reduction in cargo capacity
5058. SHRI P.R. RAJAN: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether he is aware that Air India is
reducing the cargo carrying capacity in the
flights to Gulf countries; and
(b) whether he will reconsider the
decision as it could adversely affect the
agricultural and food export from the State?
Route dispersal guidelines
5059. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether airlines companies may no
longer be forced to fly on uneconomic
routes as Government plans to
progressively do away with the route
dispersal guidelines that stipulate a
minimum number of flights to be deployed
on such routes;
(b) whether a long pending demand of
the aviation industry shall be replaced with
the creation of a separate fund to subsidise
uneconomic routes;
(c) whether this move is likely to benefit
airlines companies as they will no longer
be forced to fly on unprofitable routes; and
(d) if so, by when a final decision in this
regard is likely to be taken?

1177
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Improvement in profits of Indian
and AI
5060. SHRIMATI JAYA BACH-
CHAN: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that amidst the
gloom of rising losses in 2006 falling aviation
turbine fuel prices, rising occupancies and
yields provide a sense of optimism to the
aviation industry;
(b) if so, whether AI and Indian share
this optimism and if so, the details of
improvement in their profits; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Agencies for ground handling
operations

SWARAJ: Will the Minister of CIVIL

(a) whether it is a fact that 'Cabinet
Committee on Security' have formulated a
polic
